messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] how to install rstan master from repo?
parts:
Is it a fix that should go into RStan itself? If so,
would you mind opening an issue on stan-dev/rstan for it?
Or even submitting a pull request?

If it's a fix to R code, we might be able to get it in
before RStan 2.7.0, but if it's a fix to stan-dev/stan
or stan-dev/math, those are already frozen.

We may be releasing a 2.7.1 patch release after 2.7.0,
because I think there are some other ongoing minor details
of compiler compatibility we're still ironing out (mostly with
things like test precision and whether the Stan code actually
compiles).

- Bob

messages.author: 1f723d378f24adbb
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] how to install rstan master from repo?
parts:
Sorry, my wording was ambiguous. There is a fix (3af5981) that is
_already_ in the master, and I would like to _use_ it before it is
released.

I managed to do it in the end, the following way:

1. Clone with submodules
https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/wiki/How-to-Work-with-the-Stan-Submodule-in-rstan-Repo%3F

2. Install using devtools,

library(devtools)
devtools::install("~/path-to/rstan/StanHeaders")
devtools::install("~/path-to/rstan/rstan/rstan")

I am posting this for the archives, but maybe someone will submit
a simpler solution.

Best,

Tamas

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: how to install rstan master from repo?
parts:
On Saturday, July 18, 2015 at 11:03:22 AM UTC-4, Tamas Papp wrote:
Is there a simple way of installing the latest master branch of
rstan?  There is a fix that I would like to have before 2.7 is
released.

devtools::install_github("stan-dev/rstan", ref = "v2.7.0", subdir = "rstan/rstan", dependencies = TRUE)

will say at the end

Warning message:
Github repo contains submodules, may not function as expected!

which you can ignore.

Ben
